Flint 0.5 introduces formal visual themes: one specification can now carry
layout behavior, semantic presentation, and visual identity across an entire
chart library.

### Define the visual system once

Add `theme_spec` beside `chart_spec`. The chart spec continues to define what
the chart means; the theme defines how that meaning is presented.

```json
{
  "chart_spec": {
    "chartType": "Bar Chart",
    "encodings": {
      "x": { "field": "region" },
      "y": { "field": "revenue" }
    }
  },
  "theme_spec": "economist"
}
```

Themes participate in compilation. They can guide spacing and density, labels
and legends, axes and annotations, mark geometry, typography, color, and chart
furniture while adapting those decisions to each chart.

### Start from ten visual themes

Flint ships New York Times, Economist, Swiss, Nature, McKinsey, Datawrapper,
Power BI, Power BI Light, Pop, and Cartoon presets. The
[visual-theme explorer](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/themes)
applies each preset to the same set of charts for direct comparison.

### Create a brand theme

Pass a custom `ThemeSpec`, or inherit a built-in preset and override only the
decisions that should differ:

```json
{
  "theme_spec": {
    "extends": "economist",
    "id": "our-brand",
    "ink": {
      "series": {
        "single": "#6b3fa0"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Nested objects merge; arrays and scalar values replace inherited values. See
[Using themes](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/documentation/theme-spec)
for the complete vocabulary and examples.

### Explore ideas in Theme Lab

[Theme Lab](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/theme-lab) provides an
interactive ThemeSpec editor and a diverse chart wall, so a visual system can
be tested across chart types and data shapes rather than tuned against one
example. It includes Signal Studio, Microsoft Fluent, and People's Daily
starting points, and is available in English and Chinese.

### Use themes with agents

The MCP server adds `list_themes` so an agent can inspect the available visual
systems and their authoring guidance. The interactive MCP App also exposes a
theme picker for Vega-Lite charts. It preserves a request's custom ThemeSpec
while the user compares presets, without storing that custom theme globally.

Agents can also load the bundled `flint://theme-skill` resource or the
`author_flint_theme` prompt to translate brand guidance and visual references
into a reusable ThemeSpec.

<img width="800" alt="An agent creates an interactive grouped bar chart in the Flint MCP App" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/flint-chart/main/docs/figs/flint-mcp-experience.png" />

*The MCP App keeps chart generation, visual inspection, customization, and spec
handoff in one conversation.*

ThemeSpec is currently realized by the Vega-Lite backend. Other backends
continue to accept the shared Flint input but do not yet apply `theme_spec`.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete technical summary.
